```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(pdmS7)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
# Shows the error a call raises, as the user would see it.
says <- function(expr) {
  tryCatch({
    force(expr)
    "no error"
  }, error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
}
model <- pdm_model(area_km2 = 20)
forcing <- data.frame(rain = c(0, 5, 2, 0, 0, 1), pet = 0.05)
```

The common problems, the message pdmS7 gives, and what to do. Each message on this page is
produced by the package itself when the site is built, so it matches what you will see.

# Data

## Missing or negative inputs

```{r inputs}
says(run_pdm(model, data.frame(rain = c(1, NA), pet = 0.05)))
says(run_pdm(model, data.frame(rain = c(1, 2), pet = c(0.05, -1))))
```

The model cannot run through a gap in rain or PET, and negative values are data faults. Infill
rain by one recorded method; fill PET from a seasonal curve. [Preparing your
data](data-preparation.html), steps 2, 5 and 6.

## Rows that do not line up

```{r align}
config <- pdm_presets("standard")
says(calibrate_pdm(config, forcing, observed = c(1, 2, 3), lower = c(fc = 0.8),
                   upper = c(fc = 1.2)))
```

The forcing and the observed flow must have one row each per time step. Join them on time, not
by position, and fill missing time steps with explicit rows.

## Scores that cannot be computed

```{r scores}
says(calibrate_pdm(config, forcing, observed = rep(2, 6), lower = c(fc = 0.8),
                   upper = c(fc = 1.2), objective = "nse"))
```

NSE compares the model with the mean observed flow, so it needs flow that varies. A window that
is almost all missing, or a constant flow, usually means the wrong file or a broken gauge record.

## Times

If the model's floods arrive one step early or late on every event, the rain or the flow is
stamped at the start of the step instead of the end, or is in local time instead of UTC. Plot a
few sharp storms: flow cannot rise before the rain that causes it.

# Calibration

## Bounds and starting values

```{r bounds}
says(calibrate_pdm(config, forcing, observed = c(1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 1), lower = c(fc = 1.2),
                   upper = c(fc = 1.5)))
```

The starting value of each calibrated parameter, from the configuration, must lie inside its
bounds. Widen the bounds or change the starting configuration. `calibration_bounds()` gives
default bounds that include the standard presets.

## Parameters ending on a bound

Not an error, but a warning sign. The search was stopped by the fence, not by the data. Check
the data first (wrong area, biased rainfall, a rating change), then consider whether the bound
is physically justified. Widening a bound to let a parameter run away rarely gives a better
model. The `start_results` table of a calibration shows each start's final values.

## Starts that disagree

Several starts ending at different parameters with similar scores mean the data do not pin
those parameters down (equifinality). More starts will not fix it. Staged calibration
(`calibrate_staged()`), which fits groups of parameters to the parts of the hydrograph they
control, often helps. [Automatic calibration, explained](auto-calibration.html).

## A threshold objective with the gradient method

```{r threshold}
says(calibrate_pdm(config, forcing, observed = c(1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 1), lower = c(fc = 0.8),
                   upper = c(fc = 1.2), thresholds = c(alert = 2.5), method = "lbfgsb"))
```

Threshold scores change in steps, so a gradient method cannot follow them. Use
`method = "nelder_mead"`.

## The search found nothing valid

`No valid calibration evaluation; inspect configuration and bounds` means every trial failed to
run. Usually a combination of components and bounds that the model rejects, for example demand
recharge with a cascade groundwater store. Run the starting configuration once with `run_pdm()`:
its error says what is wrong.

# Model structure

```{r structure}
says(pdm_model(recharge = DemandRecharge(alpha = 0.5, beta = 1, qsat = 101)))
says(correct_state(pdm_model(td = 2), initial_state(pdm_model(td = 2)), 1))
```

Some components only make sense together. Demand recharge needs a single groundwater store with
room for its rate; state correction needs no outlet delay (`td = 0`), because with a delay the
latest observation reflects an earlier state. [Choosing model components](model-options.html).

# Batches

## A basin failed

`batch_status()` shows the step it reached and the reason. Fix the cause, often a data file, and
run the same `calibrate_batch()` call again: finished basins pass through in moments and the
failed one carries on from where it stopped. Use `only = "B06"` to retry just that basin.
[Calibrating many catchments](many-catchments.html).

## A lock left behind

If R was stopped while writing to a project, the next write may report removing a stale lock.
That is expected: the package clears a lock left by a session that no longer exists.

# The calibration log

## Not enough years to hold back

```{r wettest}
time <- seq(as.POSIXct("2020-10-01", tz = "UTC"), by = 86400, length.out = 3 * 365)
says(wettest_years(time, rep(1, length(time)), n = 2))
```

By default `register_data()` holds back the two wettest water years, which needs a record of
at least five years with half of each observed. For a shorter record, set `wettest_years = 1`
or `0` and say why in the registration's reasoning. Without a `time` column in the forcing,
registration refuses for the same reason: water years need dates. If holding back the wettest
year leaves the validation window almost empty, lengthen the window; the message names it.
[Larger floods](extrapolation.html).

## A data file has changed

`Registered ... file has changed since registration` means a data file no longer matches the
checksum taken when it was registered. Someone edited or replaced it. Do not carry on: restore
the original, or register the new file as new data with a note explaining why.

## An entry no longer reproduces

`... no longer reproduces its recorded output` means rerunning a logged configuration gives a
different flow. Usually the package or R has changed since the entry was written.
`verify_project(project, rerun = TRUE)` names what changed. Recalibrate under the new version, or
run the old version to reproduce the record.

## A Steward cannot sign off

```{r self, eval=FALSE}
sign_off_project(project, "Accepted.", reviewed)
#> Error: You wrote calibration entries in this project; another Steward must sign off
```

By design. A Steward who took part in the calibration cannot sign it off. Ask another Steward,
or a Delegated Steward. [Reviewing a calibration](steward-guide.html).

# Forecasting

```{r forecast}
says(pdm_hindcast(model, forcing, observed = c(1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 1), window = 6:6))
```

A hindcast needs room for forecast origins inside the window, with at least one step after
each. Widen the window or shorten `every_h`. [Testing forecasts with
hindcasts](hindcasts.html).

# Still stuck

Check the function's help page (`?calibrate_pdm` and so on), then the [Glossary](glossary.html)
for any unfamiliar term. If the package itself seems wrong, report it with a small example that
reproduces the problem on the
[issue tracker](https://github.com/JonPayneEA/PDMS7/issues).
